baseline.method: Independently read local git HEAD bytes and compared with the author's original GitHub-source binding; no new remote retrieval by this reviewer.

findings.finding: require_layout defaults to False. Existing four-stage/current-round/draw-revision/public-state/source-PNG/hash/pixel-recomputation checks remain in place. The default call does not require new sidecars or rewrite historical evidence.

The separately owned current Studio verifier explicitly calls verify_cards_front_faces(cards, surface_evidence, require_layout=True). Its AST contract allows only that additional keyword while retaining the existing Android identity/state/lifecycle assertion body. This is a source inspection, not a full Studio integration test.

For each of the final two actual frame entries the before/after layout must use the exact capture-derived filename, be a regular non-symlink file of at most 128 KiB, match its raw SHA256, and parse identically to the embedded observation. The before/after JSON and their raw SHA256 must agree.

The actual PNG is passed again to require_cards_face_pixels with the checked layout. The helper validates actual Android observation origin, current public identity/state, render-view/system-inset intersection and independently projected mesh corners. The publisher does not enable fixture acceptance.

The recomputed canonical layout hash and integer layout sequence must equal the stage report and each other in both final consecutive frames. Existing actual draw/card-conservation and acknowledgment bindings remain required.

New tests clearly label synthetic parser/state bindings; both historical and renderer geometry fixtures are used. Their success is not evidence that a new Android APK has passed Cards or that a physical Fold7 was measured.

existing_logs_read.interpretation: Original verifier lacks the required Studio layout contract; several repeated failures are expected-message mismatches against the old PNG-report equality rejection, not eleven separately established production faults.
Six new methods and all eight existing legacy methods, as recorded by the author. Not rerun by this reviewer.
